newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wages data boosts hopes for rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Australian wages data boosts hopes for rate cut.

text.p: Australian bonds reached two-year highs on Thursday after low annual wage rise figures appeared to strengthen the case for an official interest rate cut.
Figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed that average weekly wages rose by 3.5 percent in the year to August, slightly below the 3.7 percent predicted by analysts.
The data followed news on Wednesday that consumer inflation, at an annual 2.1 percent, was at its lowest for two years.
Financial markets were watching Thursday's figure closely after a warning last week by the policy-making Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) that wages were rising too fast.

Reacting to the news, the December 10-year bond futures contract set a new high of 92.565, its highest for more than two years, in a demonstration that the market expects lower interest rates by the end of the year.
The Australian dollar fell back slightly while the share market index was up almost one percent on Wednesday's close.
Economists said the wages data increased pressure for a cut in the official interest rate from its current seven percent, but said the RBA might hold its fire for another month.
"I think this number well and truly paves the way for a (rate) cut in the December quarter," said Dresdner chief economist Rob Henderson.
